record.original_question: Do there exist topological spaces X and Y such that every separately continuous function f: X × Y -> R is point-wise discontinuous, meaning that C(f) is dense in X × Y, while at the same time there exists a separately continuous function f_0: X × Y -> R that is not quasi-continuous?

evidence.quote: Upon some additional conditions on spaces X, Y and Z every separately continuous function f : X × Y → Z is quasi-continuous and point-wise discontinuous (i.e. C(f) is dense in X × Y ).

Problem 7.3. Do there exist topological spaces X and Y such that every separately continuous function f : X × Y → R is point-wise discontinuous and simultaneously there is a separately continuous function f0 : X × Y → R which is not quasi-continuous?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let X and Y be topological spaces and let ℝ denote the real line with its standard topology. A function f: X × Y → ℝ is said to be separately continuous if for every fixed x₀ ∈ X the map y ↦ f(x₀, y) is continuous on Y, and for every fixed y₀ ∈ Y the map x ↦ f(x, y₀) is continuous on X. Denote by C(f) the set of points of (joint) continuity of f. The function f is called point-wise discontinuous if C(f) is dense in X × Y. The function f is called quasi-continuous at a point (x₀, y₀) ∈ X × Y if for every open neighborhood W of f(x₀, y₀) in ℝ and every open neighborhood U of (x₀, y₀) in X × Y there exists a nonempty open set V ⊆ U such that f(V) ⊆ W; f is quasi-continuous if it is quasi-continuous at every point of X × Y.

Question: Do there exist topological spaces X and Y with the following two properties simultaneously?
(a) Every separately continuous function f: X × Y → ℝ is point-wise discontinuous (that is, C(f) is dense in X × Y).
(b) There exists a separately continuous function f₀: X × Y → ℝ that is not quasi-continuous.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search surfaces extensive work by Maslyuchenko and collaborators on separate continuity, point-wise discontinuity, and quasi-continuity, including generalizations to Maslyuchenko-valued functions and results on the structure of discontinuity sets. However, no source located explicitly resolves the specific question of whether there exist spaces X, Y such that every separately continuous f: X × Y → ℝ is point-wise discontinuous while some separately continuous f₀: X × Y → ℝ fails to be quasi-continuous. The status appears unverified by available evidence.

status_evidence.title: Quasicontinuous and separately continuous functions with values in Maslyuchenko spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Generalizes classical results about quasicontinuous and separately continuous functions to functions with values in Maslyuchenko spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Active research line on quasi-continuity vs separate continuity, but does not explicitly answer the stated problem.

status_evidence.title: Separately continuous functions with a given rectangular set of points of discontinuity
status_evidence.snippet: Constructions of separately continuous functions with prescribed discontinuity sets.
status_evidence.claim: Related constructions exist, but no resolution of the simultaneous condition (a)+(b) was located.
